## Natural history notes

A small orange-brown grass skipper characterized by its rounded wings, sturdy body, hooked antennae, and pale translucent spots on the forewings. In Florida, it is found in open grassy habitats such as prairies, marsh edges, wet meadows, roadsides, fields, pine flatwoods, and other sunny areas where grasses and nectar plants are available. Adults visit flowers for nectar and often perch low in vegetation, while the caterpillars feed on grasses, using folded or tied grass blades as shelters during development.
